questions.q: Why does self-attention get expensive for long inputs?
options: The score table has n × n entries.
why: Correct: cost grows with n squared.

questions.q: A window has 336 steps. Patch length 16, stride 8, no padding. How many patches?
What is channel independence in PatchTST?
options: Each variable is processed on its own as a univariate series, with shared weights.
Each variable gets its own separate model with different weights.
Variables are mixed in the first layer.
why: The weights are shared across channels.

questions.q: Which model makes each variable one token?
why: Informer uses time-step tokens with ProbSparse attention.
PatchTST uses patches of one channel.

questions.q: Data: 300 related sensors, only 96 time steps each. Which design is more natural to try first, and why?
options: iTransformer: 300 variate tokens, attention learns relations between sensors.
PatchTST: patches are needed because the series is very long.
why: Correct reasoning, but compare with baselines.
The series is short; patching helps long series. Also, channel independence ignores relations.

questions.q: A paper shows a new Transformer beats others on ETTh1. What do you do before adopting it?
options: Adopt it, the paper is peer-reviewed.
Reproduce on your data with a time-based backtest against seasonal naive and a linear model, and include cost.
why: Benchmarks may not match your data.
